results.summary: A lighthouse lens uses multiple thin glass rings to bend the light, making it more efficient and allowing it to focus more light on the sea. This lens is much lighter than a single, thick piece of curved glass, and it can capture more of the lamp's light. The lens turns slowly on a bed of liquid mercury or on ball bearings, driven by a clockwork motor, to capture the light across the sea.
